_provenance.derived_from: 168 Cambridge published mark schemes, 2020-2025 (84 x 0450, 84 x 0455)
_provenance.derivation_policy: structure only. No mark-scheme wording is reproduced in learner-facing output.
_provenance.validation: per-paper tariff sums reconcile: 0450 = 80; 0455 Paper 2 = 110 printed (30 Section A + 4 x 20 Section B, candidate answers three, for 90).
_provenance.verification: Every shape below was re-counted against the raw mark-scheme text, per question block, not per file. The percentage on each shape is the share of that command-word-and-tariff population that carries the stated structure. A shape under 90% carries its exceptions.

0455.subject: Cambridge IGCSE Economics

2.structure: Section A one compulsory 30-mark source-based question; Section B three of four 20-mark questions

shape: two creditable elements of the definition

shapes.guard: if more than two are given, only the first are considered

shape: four distinct, correct, linked statements, one mark each
shapes.note: the most common question form on Paper 2: a 2 x 2 grid
shapes.verified: This is point-marked from a pool, not a fixed grid. 31% state the pool as two reasons each developed once; 36% open with "logical explanation which might include" and list far more creditable statements than there are marks; 8% use a variant of the identify-plus-explain wording. The rule that fits all of them: one mark per distinct linked statement, up to four.
shapes.guard: A statement that only restates the one before it earns nothing. Each of the four has to add something — a reason, a consequence, or a further step in the chain.

shape: original curves correctly drawn and labelled
the correct curve shifted in the correct direction
shapes.guard: stating that price moves from P1 to P2 earns nothing on its own

shape_chain: consequence for the economic agent named
shapes.guard: Quoting figures is description, not analysis. State the relationship, give a direct comparison as evidence, then give the reason. Examiners refuse figure-quoting explicitly.
shape: one mark per distinct linked statement, from an open pool
each statement carries its reason; a bare assertion is not analysis
shapes.verified: 94% of 6-mark Analyse questions open with "coherent analysis which might include" and list a median of 17 creditable statements for 6 marks, so the pool is wide and the marking is point-by-point. 16% require a diagram as well as the written analysis. The chain below is how the mark schemes structure their own lists, not a phrase they state.

requires: a reasoned discussion that accurately examines both sides of the economic argument
clear and logical analysis to evaluate economic issues and situations
bands.note: one side may carry more depth than the other

requires: a reasoned discussion using economic information and clear analysis
bands.limits: may lack depth; development may be one-sided

shapes.verified: 95% are level-banded over three bands. 96% require the top band to examine BOTH sides of the argument. 78% lay the answer out as "why it might" then "why it might not", which is the skeleton to write to.

shapes.note: same two-sided architecture at a lower tariff

refusals: restating the figures is description, not analysis
a diagram on its own earns nothing where a written point is required
an example is not a definition
a point credited once is not credited again in other words
a near-miss term is refused where the syllabus term is specific (GDP per head is not GDP)
